originalTitle: Sudan's invisible children - born in war with no legal identity
title: Sudan's Special Babies: Everyone Deserves a Name!
content:
Hello, my amazing friends! It's your kid-friendly reporter from Africa, here to share a very important story with you. Today, we are going to talk about some special babies in a country called Sudan. Sudan is a big country in Africa, just like many of our homes. Sometimes, when grown-ups fight, it's called a war. War can be very, very sad. It makes things hard for everyone, especially for children. In Sudan, because of the war, some babies are born, but they don't have a very important piece of paper. This paper is super special, and it's called a birth certificate. These babies are sometimes called "invisible children" because without this paper, it's like nobody officially knows they are here. But guess what? We want to make sure everyone knows they are here, and that they are super important!

What's a Birth Certificate? It's Super Important!

Imagine you have a name, like "Sarah" or "David." And you have a birthday, like January 1st. A birth certificate is like a special card that grown-ups get for you when you are just a tiny baby. This card has your name, your birthday, and where you were born. It also says who your mommy and daddy are. It’s like your first official identity card! **Did you know?** Almost every person in the world has a birth certificate! It's super important for your whole life. It proves that you are you! It's like having a special ticket that says, "Hello world, I am here!" This paper helps you do many things when you grow up. It helps you go to school, see a doctor, and even get your very first real job when you are a grown-up. Without it, things can be very difficult. Think of it like trying to play a game without knowing the rules – it's just not fair!

Why Are Some Babies Missing Their Special Paper?

Now, let's talk about why some babies in Sudan don't have this special paper. When there is a war, like in Sudan, things can get very messy and scary. Families might have to leave their homes very fast to find a safe place. Houses might get broken, and important papers, like birth certificates, can get lost or destroyed. Sometimes, in wars, very, very sad things happen. Some mothers get hurt, and they might have a baby because of these very sad things. It can be very hard for these mothers to get a birth certificate for their babies because things are broken, or they might feel too scared or sad to ask for help. They might not even have the papers needed to prove who they are themselves. Imagine if your school records were suddenly gone, and nobody knew which class you were in! It's a bit like that, but much more serious. Getting a birth certificate needs grown-ups to fill out forms and go to offices, but in a war, offices might be closed, or the grown-ups who can help are not there. It's a very difficult situation for new moms and tiny babies. **Did you know?** When there is a war, it's not just homes that get broken. Sometimes, the way countries keep records also gets broken. This makes it hard to help people get their important papers.

What Happens When You Don't Have This Paper?

So, what happens to these "invisible children" who don't have a birth certificate? It's like living in a world where you don't have a name tag, and nobody knows who you are. First, it can be very hard for them to go to school. Imagine not being able to learn to read or write because you don't have a paper to prove how old you are or where you were born. Education is super important, and every child deserves to learn! Second, it can be hard to go to the doctor or hospital if they get sick. If you don't have a birth certificate, it's harder for grown-ups to give you the right medicines or help because they don't have your official information. Everyone deserves to be healthy and strong! Third, when they grow up, it's hard to get a job. If you want to work and help your family, you need to prove who you are. Without this paper, it's like trying to get a job when you are just a ghost! Fourth, they can't travel easily. If they need to go to another town or even another country to be safe, they might not be allowed to go because they don't have any official proof of who they are. It's a really big problem that makes children feel like they don't quite belong. Every child should feel loved, safe, and seen. Not having a birth certificate makes it hard for the government and kind organizations to protect these children and make sure they get everything they need. It's like they are missing a very important puzzle piece in their life. **Did you know?** There are millions of children around the world who do not have a birth certificate. Many of them live in places where there is war or other problems.

Helping Our Invisible Friends

But here's the good news, my friends! Many kind people and big organizations are working very hard to help these "invisible children." They know how important it is for every child to have a name and a birth certificate. These wonderful grown-ups are trying to reach out to mothers and families in Sudan. They are setting up special places where families can go to get help with the paperwork. They are explaining to people why birth certificates are so important and how to get them, even when things are difficult because of the war. Some organizations are even trying to change the rules a little bit, so it's easier for babies born in very difficult situations to get their special paper. They are working with governments to make sure every child is counted and recognized. It's a big job, but many kind hearts are working together like a super team! **Did you know?** International organizations like UNICEF (which helps children all over the world!) are working hard to make sure every child gets a birth certificate, especially in places like Sudan.

Every Child Deserves to Shine!

So, what can we learn from this, my little friends? We learn that every single child in the world is special and deserves to be seen. Every child deserves to have a name, a birthday, and a special paper that says, "Here I am!" It reminds us to be kind to everyone, no matter where they come from or what problems they might have faced. We can help by learning about these stories and telling our grown-ups. We can also remember to be thankful for our own birth certificates and all the things they help us do, like go to school and visit the doctor. The children in Sudan, whether they have a birth certificate or not, are just like us. They love to play, they love to learn, and they want to be safe and happy. Let's all hope and work for a world where every child is visible, protected, and has all the papers they need to shine brightly! We want to make sure that no child ever feels invisible. They are all super stars!
summary: Because of war in Sudan, some babies are born without a birth certificate, which makes their lives very hard, but many kind people and organizations are working to help them get this important paper.
whyMatters: This matters because every child in the world deserves a name, a birthday, and official papers to prove who they are, so they can go to school, visit the doctor, and grow up safe and happy.

originalTitle: Netanyahu mulls Saudi, Turkiye, Pakistan pact as Israeli elections loom
title: Countries Making New Friend Promises!
content:
Hello, wonderful friends! It's me, your friendly news reporter for Africa! I'm here to tell you about some important news happening far away, but it's like a big story that everyone should know. Let's make it super simple and fun!

What's Happening Far Away?

Imagine you and your very best friends decide to always help each other. If someone tries to bother one of you, all your friends will stand together to protect them. That's a bit like what some big countries have just done!

Meet Our Friend Countries

We have three big countries that have made a special promise. Let's learn a little bit about them! First, there's a country called Saudi Arabia. It's really big and has lots and lots of sand, like a huge desert! They have amazing camels there, which are super cool animals. Did you know? Saudi Arabia has a very important city called Mecca. Many people from all over the world visit Mecca for special prayers. Then there's Turkiye, which some people used to call Turkey. It's a country that sits in two places at once – partly in Europe and partly in Asia! It has beautiful beaches and yummy food. Did you know? Turkiye is famous for a super sweet pastry called baklava! It's made with many thin layers of dough, nuts, and syrup. Delicious! And the third country is Pakistan. It's a country with very tall mountains, like some of the highest in the whole wide world! They have many different languages spoken there, which is pretty neat. Did you know? The second highest mountain in the world, K2, is partly in Pakistan! Only Mount Everest is taller!

A New Team Promise!

These three countries – Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan – have made a special promise to each other. We call this a 'pact.' It's like a big team agreement, just like when you and your friends agree to play a game together. They promise to help keep each other safe. This promise is all about 'defense.' Defense means protecting yourselves, your homes, your family, and your country from any trouble. If someone tries to cause trouble for one country, the others will stand up and help them. It's like having a superhero team where everyone watches out for each other! They want to feel safer together.

Who Is Watching Closely?

Now, there's another country called Israel. It's also in the same part of the world, not too far from Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. The people in Israel are watching this new friendship very, very closely. In Israel, there's a very important leader named Mr. Netanyahu. He's like the head teacher or the captain of the whole country. He has to think very hard about what this new friendship means for Israel.

Time for Choices: Elections!

Soon, the grown-ups in Israel will have 'elections.' This is like when you choose your class captain at school. Everyone gets to vote for who they want to lead their country and make the big decisions. Because elections are coming soon, Mr. Netanyahu and the other leaders in Israel have to be extra, extra careful about every decision they make. They want to do what is best and safest for their country and its people. Did you know? When countries have elections, it means the people get to choose their leaders. This is a very important part of how many countries work!

What Does It All Mean? We Don't Know Yet!

So, this new big friendship between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan is a new thing in the world. And what it will mean for everyone is a bit like a mystery. We don't know for sure what will happen next! Will this new team make things calmer in that part of the world? Or will it make other countries think differently about their own friendships? Mr. Netanyahu is thinking very hard about all these questions for Israel. He is trying to figure out the best and smartest way for Israel to respond to this new big promise between its neighbours.

Why Is This Important For Us In Africa?

You might be thinking, 'Why is this important for us, all the way here in Africa?' Well, when big countries make big decisions, it can sometimes make waves all around the world! Imagine throwing a stone into a big pond. The ripples spread out and touch everything in the water. So, what happens in other parts of the world can sometimes affect us too, even if we are far away from Saudi Arabia or Israel. It reminds us that all countries are connected, like a big global family. We all hope for peace and friendship everywhere, so everyone can live happily and safely. Did you know? The world is like one big neighbourhood! What happens in one part can sometimes affect other parts, like how the weather in one place can change the weather somewhere else!

Hoping for Peace and Friendship!

We always hope that countries will be good friends and help each other, just like we try to be good friends in school and in our communities. Talking nicely and being kind are very important for countries too. This helps everyone live in peace and happiness, which is what we all want! So, to recap, three big countries – Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan – have made a big promise to protect each other. Israel and its leader, Mr. Netanyahu, are watching closely, especially because they have elections coming up. It's a big story, and we will keep watching to see what happens next. Remember, being friendly and peaceful is always the best way! That's all for now from your friendly African news reporter! Stay curious and keep learning!
summary: Three big countries, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan, have made a new promise to protect each other, and Israel's leader is thinking carefully about what this means, especially with elections coming soon.
whyMatters: When big countries make new friendships or plans, it can change things for many other countries around the world, making the global family either more peaceful or a bit more uncertain.
